question.worked_solution:
Recall that if ${X}_{1}$ and ${X}_{2}$ are independent random variables, where ${X}_{1}∼N({\mu }_{1},{\sigma }_{1}^{2})$ and ${X}_{2}∼N({\mu }_{2},{\sigma }_{2}^{2}),$ and $a$ and $b$ are constants, then 

$$
a{X}_{1}+b{X}_{2}∼N(a{\mu }_{1}+b{\mu }_{2},{a}^{2}{\sigma }_{1}^{2}+{b}^{2}{\sigma }_{2}^{2}).
$$

Since ${X}_{1}$ and ${X}_{2}$ are independent, the distribution of $Y$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}Y={X}_{1}-{X}_{2} & ∼N({\mu }_{1}-{\mu }_{2},{\sigma }_{1}^{2}+{\sigma }_{2}^{2}) \\  & ∼N(20-2,200+25) \\  & ∼N(18,225).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $Y$ is normally distributed with mean $\mu =18$ and standard deviation $\sigma =\sqrt{225}=15.$ 

We want to find $P(Y>1.8).$ Thus, we convert $Y$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y>1.8) & =P(Z>\frac{1.8-18}{15}) \\  & =P(Z>-1.08) \\  & =1-Φ(-1.08)\end{aligned}
$$

Using the $z$-table, we see that

$$
Φ(-1.08)≈0.1401.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y>1.8) & =1-Φ(-1.08) \\  & =1-0.1401 \\  & ≈0.86.\end{aligned}
$$
